story_type: sailor hit by the boom far offshore, Jayhawk hovers over the sailboat, filmed from the escort aircraft
hook: Hit by his own boom, 140 miles out to sea.
narration: A hundred and forty miles out to sea, a sailor was hit by his boat's main boom.
His crew called the Coast Guard by satellite phone at about six thirty-five in the morning.
A Jayhawk crew from Air Station Cape Cod flew out and came to a hover over the sailboat.
The tall mast is the danger. The cable has to stay clear of it and its rigging.
The crew brought him up off the deck and turned for the coast.
outcome: And the injured sailor was flown to Rhode Island Hospital in Providence.
title: Hit by the boom, 140 miles out
description:
On June 29, 2010, a Coast Guard Air Station Cape Cod Jayhawk crew hoisted a crewman who had been struck by the main boom from the sailboat Bombardino, about 140 miles south of Nantucket, and flew him to Rhode Island Hospital.
